claim: NullPropagatedOperands recurses into both operands of every SqlBinaryExpression, but AndAlso, OrElse and Coalesce are legal operators there and none propagates NULL, so operands reached through them are added to the set and DropNotNullChecks deletes a load-bearing IS NOT NULL guard. Queries then return wrong values and, in WHERE position, wrong rows.
raw: `NullPropagatedOperands` treats `AndAlso`/`OrElse` operands as null-propagating, so a load-bearing `IS NOT NULL` guard is deleted and queries silently return wrong values and wrong rows

claim: All five added tests have value-typed THEN results (unary Not, int? addition, string concatenation), so none reaches the AndAlso/OrElse arms of NullPropagatedOperands. The failing shape class is entirely uncovered and the suite passes with the critical defect fully present.
raw: none of the five new tests exercises a boolean-valued `THEN` result, so the failing shape class is entirely uncovered

claim: RestoreNullValueColumnsList is passed the non-nullable column counter (currentNonNullableColumnsCount) instead of the null-value column counter. The two lists are independent, so when their counts differ this over- or under-truncates _nullValueColumns, leaking or discarding column nullability facts across when-clauses.
raw: `RestoreNullValueColumnsList` is passed the non-nullable column counter

claim: IsNull(elseResult) is false when elseResult is a C# null reference, i.e. when the CaseExpression has no ELSE clause at all. Since SQL treats a missing ELSE as ELSE NULL, the semantically identical shape is skipped, so the optimization applies inconsistently depending on how the tree was built.
raw: `IsNull(elseResult)` is `false` when `elseResult` is a C# `null` reference

claim: When the whole test is dropped and clause.Result is returned, the nullable out-parameter still carries true from the null ELSE constant even if clause.Result is itself non-nullable. Conservative but can cost an unnecessary downstream null compensation.
raw: when the whole test is dropped and `clause.Result` is returned, the `nullable` out-parameter still carries `true`

claim: NullPropagatedOperands has no comment stating the invariant it maintains (e is in the set only if e IS NULL implies the root expression IS NULL). That invariant is the entire correctness argument for the feature and the method name misleads about its meaning.
raw: `NullPropagatedOperands` has no comment stating the invariant it maintains

claim: The new baselines assert SQL text only for SQL Server, although the rewrite lives in the shared relational processor and changes result semantics. At least one of the new cases warrants a SQLite baseline too, where concatenation and AND/OR render differently.
raw: the new baselines assert SQL text only for SQL Server

claim: COALESCE arguments could be wrongly collected as null-propagating in the SqlFunctionExpression arm. Rejected: SqlExpressionFactory.Coalesce constructs it with argumentsPropagateNullability [false, false] and a probe confirmed the guard is retained.

HashSet<SqlExpression> lookups could fail because SqlExpression uses reference equality. Rejected: ColumnExpression, SqlBinaryExpression, SqlUnaryExpression and SqlExpression all override Equals/GetHashCode structurally including TypeMapping, so lookups succeed.
raw: [false] `HashSet<SqlExpression>` lookups fail because `SqlExpression` uses reference equality

claim: Possible index-out-of-range on func.Arguments[i] when ArgumentsPropagateNullability is shorter. Rejected: SqlFunctionExpression's constructor throws on a count mismatch and MemberNotNullWhen on IsNiladic makes both non-null on the guarded path.

func.Instance! could dereference null if a function is constructed with InstancePropagatesNullability true but a null Instance. No constructor guard ruling this out was found; reachability unconfirmed.

Recursion through Not/Negate/Convert in the unary allowlist could be unsound. Rejected: all three propagate NULL in three-valued SQL and probes of ~NullableIntA, -NullableIntA and CAST(LEN(...) AS int) produced correct results after optimization.

A baseline update could bake in a wrong rewrite across the five sibling baseline files. Rejected: each of the five distinct SQL shapes removed is null-propagating in the dropped operand, so each baseline change is correct.
raw: [false] a baseline update bakes in a wrong rewrite

claim: String concatenation baselines assume SQL Server CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL is ON. Rejected: OFF is deprecated by SQL Server and already unsupported by EF Core's existing concatenation handling (AddNullConcatenationProtection), so the change adds no new dependency.
raw: String concatenation baselines assume SQL Server `CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL` is `ON`

claim: The xor shape (x.NullableBoolA != null ? (bool?)(a ^ b) : null) generates a three-column projection on SQLite. Confirmed identical on the base commit, so unrelated to this diff and outside norm scope.
raw: The `xor` shape generates a three-column projection on SQLite
